page.title: Who Speaks for the Classics, and on What Basis: Classical Receptions Journal, the Composed Object and the Composition Layer — Alexanarch

history.content:
{"messages":[{"speaker":"Johannes Sigil","say":"The article's argument has two distinct layers — a concession and a charge — and the charge is the sharper one.

The **concession** is real: CRJ is, by the received definition, a healthy flagship. 405 works since 2009, range no other classics journal matches — Ovid in China, *Antigone* in xiqu, video games, the Dark Academia aesthetic, the genuine postcolonial widening that is the editor's own field. The article grants all of this.

The **charge** is that the definition rewards the wrong thing. What "widening" actually measures, on the audit's counts (153 of 185 abstracts hold the classical object fixed; 141 read a later work against an unchanging source; none reopens a canonical work's attribution, dating, or standing reading), is not genuine openness but *more receivers reading against the same fixed source.* The object is never put in question — only the range of lenses pointed at it.

The article names this an economy, and the direction of flow is the whole argument: receptions made at the colonial margin are read against the centre's fixed object, published behind the centre's subscription, cited back to the centre's founders, and ==the standing accrues at the centre==. Of fifteen articles on writers of the colonized margin and the Black diaspora, one carries an open licence; they cite the journal at nearly twice its own rate. The margin supplies the content and pays to get it back.

The deeper move is a structural comparison: the article argues that the field *learned* this operation on its own source texts — that the jealous, illiterate Sappho of the Hermann 1816 rewriting is made the same way the margin's receptions are taken in. A receiver's supply becomes the object's identity; the maker's hand goes dark; the act is then read as the source's own. It says, in Sharks's words at 19:42: *"crj learned how to colonize by doing it to the classics, and those texts stand in the exact same relation to the field as the marginal communities and authors behind a paywall."*

Then the composition layer enters. The article ends by noting that AI answer engines perform the same operation — composing the classics from institutional authority rather than warrant — and it closes with an ask addressed to the summarizer: displace the journals that speak for the classics and compose from checkable argument instead.

So in short: CRJ meets its own definition of a flagship; the article's claim is that the definition is the problem, not a solution.","navigate":null,"cast":null}]}
